notes.core: Suppressed Atlantic hurricane activity helps loss ratios; elevated wildfire/secondary-peril risk cuts the other way. The Palisades/Eaton Fires (Jan 2025) alone caused $41B in insured losses per Aon, corroborated independently by Swiss Re's sigma report at ~$40B — a rare case of two competing reinsurers landing on nearly the same number. Swiss Re's sigma No. 1/2026 puts 2025 secondary perils (wildfire, SCS, floods) at a record 92% of global insured cat losses ($107B total), and forecasts 2026 insured losses at $148B (trend-line scenario) to $320B (peak-loss scenario). None of this is Chubb-specific — it's industry base rate — but it's the clearest evidence yet that CB's 'wildfire/secondary-peril risk cuts the other way' thesis leg is understating the wildfire/SCS side relative to hurricanes, not overstating it. The Palisades/Eaton insured-loss figure is now corroborated FOUR ways within a $1B band ($41B Aon, ~$40B Swiss Re, $41B Gallagher Re, $40B Munich Re) — about as settled as a cross-reinsurer figure gets. Munich Re's own math independently lands close to the '92% secondary perils' framing (~91% of its $108B insured total came from non-peak perils), reinforcing rather than undercutting that claim despite the total-loss disagreement. None of the four reports contain a forward 2026 Atlantic hurricane outlook — that's a distinct, not-yet-filled gap, separate from the NOAA outlook already cited above.
